qs.q: A 35-year-old intravenous drug user presents with a painful, firm nodule in the axilla that has developed a central yellow head and fluctuance over several days. What is the primary pathological structure involved in this furuncle?
o: A hair follicle and surrounding tissue
qs.e: A furuncle is defined as an abscess involving a hair follicle, typically caused by Staphylococcus aureus. Apocrine gland involvement is characteristic of hidradenitis suppurativa rather than a solitary furuncle.
